nodes.title: RAPID - appearance-based 3D pose tracking (cv2.rapid, opencv-contrib)
widgets_values:
Given a wireframe 3D model (vertices + triangles), a camera matrix and a rough initial pose, cv2.rapid samples control points along the model's projected silhouette, shoots a search line along each point's normal and snaps every line to the strongest intensity edge - then solvePnP turns the matched pairs into a refined pose. That is the engine inside the OLS/GO silhouette trackers.

Sources: OpenCV documentation, contrib module 'rapid' (docs.opencv.org -> group__rapid); HodaÅˆ, Michel, Neumann - appearance-based tracking (GO-RT), the method this module implements. No asset files: the object is a synthetic cube whose observation THIS CANVAS renders with the very same cv2.rapid.drawWireframe node the tracker refines against - ground truth stays data.

nodes.title: [CV Rapid Pose Refine] MANUAL PIPELINE: CV Rapid Pose Refine
MEASURED CONTRACT on this scene
widgets_values: MEASURED CONTRACT on this scene (num=150 control points, len=30 px search lines): a perturbed pose ~20 px off reprojects about HALF as close after ONE track step and keeps improving for 2-3 steps, then oscillates - rapid is a SHORT-HORIZON refiner: feed it each frame's last pose, never a guess from scratch. rmsd (mean gradient locked onto; higher = stronger edges found) and score (its sum over all lines) fall together as the pose degrades - they are the per-step confidence the real OLS/GO trackers gate on, and there is NO found=false path: far enough off-model the raw nodes raise instead.

nodes.title: How this canvas is laid out
widgets_values:
Left to right inside every band, top to bottom down the canvas.

1. THE SCENE builds the cube, the camera and the OBSERVATION this canvas renders with the very same 'cv2 rapid drawWireframe' node the tracker refines against - ground truth stays data.

2. THE PERTURBED START is the pose the tracker is handed, ~20 px off.

3. LANE 1 chains two ONE-SHOT 'cv2 rapid rapid' steps and overlays them (red = perturbed, blue = refined) with the per-step ratio / rmsd readouts.

4. LANE 2 rebuilds the same refinement from the five pipeline nodes inside the subgraph 'CV Rapid Pose Refine' (yellow overlay). It draws the search lines, and reads the line bundle as DATA rather than as a picture: 'CV Chart Matrix' shows one row per control point and one column per pixel of offset along the search normal, where the single 255 cell in each row is the edge cv2.rapid matched (nothing in the scene reaches 255 - the canvas is 20, the filled face 200, the edges 235). Beside it, the two per-line numbers the aggregate readouts average away: WHERE each line matched (30 = it did not move off the silhouette) and HOW STRONG that edge was.

5. SCORE IT reprojects both poses and compares them with the TRUE projection, in pixels.
